title: Plasma Levels of Interleukin-6 Mediate Neurocognitive Performance in Older Breast Cancer Survivors: The Thinking and Living with Cancer Study
notes: TLC study prospective cohort; women >=60 years; breast cancer stage 0-III; pre-systemic therapy baseline to 60 months follow-up. Mediation analysis: Survivor status → cytokines → cognition. Table 2 reports mediation model path coefficients (βa=cancer→cytokine, βb=cytokine→cognition, βab=indirect). APE composite = attention + processing speed + executive function (TMT-A, TMT-B, SDMT, COWAT). LM domain = learning/memory. IL-6 and TNF-alpha significantly mediate survivor→APE relationship. IL-6 mediation βab=-0.023 SE=0.009 p=0.01 survives Bonferroni correction. LM domain: no survivor/control differences, no mediation. Also measured IL-8, IL-10, IFN-gamma. Controlled for age, race, education, site, anxiety, depression, BMI, comorbidities, time.
null_findings: LM (Learning/Memory) domain: no survivor vs control differences in mediation model
IL-8 → APE: not associated (βb not reported as significant)
IFN-gamma → APE: not associated (βb not reported as significant)
IL-6 → LM: not mediated (no survivor/control LM differences)
